bounds: Three monotonically allocated sequence values, retained-row deletion, one captured fence, a one-row page capacity, one replacement epoch and one blocked projection identity.
fairness: PagesFinish assumes weakly fair page requests, a stable matching epoch and eventually projectable retained rows. Corrupt or oversized head rows can continue failing until repaired or explicitly removed.
limitations: The finite capacity one represents the item/byte page boundary. Real tests check the actual encoded envelope and native byte limits without truncating records.
A sequence cursor can skip deleted/expired/superseded rows when no retained row exists at that sequence. The fence remains fixed across later appends.
Malformed arbitrary cursor numbers, unknown record fields and Unicode byte encoding are checked by existing implementation tests, outside the finite value domain.
Changing the inbox epoch invalidates old cursors. After that error the client must explicitly begin a new snapshot, which is outside this one-cursor model.
